name: Mud Brown
lede: Mud Brown is a dark, dull olive-brown first recorded as a swatch name in the xkcd 2010 crowd color survey, a darker, browner member of the plain [[mud]] family.

sections.title: A darker shade of mud
sections.body:
Our library traces this exact name only to the xkcd 2010 crowd survey, which asked thousands of volunteers to label swatches in their own words [1]. It belongs to a family of names built on the plain word [[mud]], the lighter base color from which this swatch is a darker, browner variant [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary's nearest block is "moderate olive brown," 3.9 units from that block's centre [1].

Its nearest named neighbors are [[field-drab|Field Drab]] and [[olive-mud|Olive Mud]], each 4.8 units away and lighter [2]. [[japanese-bush-warbler-brown|Japanese Bush Warbler Brown]] sits 5.3 units out, duller [2]. Measured in LCH it reads lightness 32, chroma 36, a dark warm brown [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 1,521 of 23,781 paintings, about 6.4 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 795 [3]. It is more common than 88 percent of the named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1600s, at 3.8 percent of the 6,394 paintings from that century (243 paintings) [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone across its 795 occurrences [3]. Paulus Potter is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 8 of his 28 works here, 5.2 times the baseline rate (4.0 times as photographed) [3]. The earliest archive match dates to the year 799, 1,211 years before the name's 2010 record; that gap marks a look-alike hue in an aged, varnished photograph, not evidence that the name or pigment is that old [3]. It shares canvases with Muddy Brown and Mustard Brown more than chance, at 11.7 and 5.3 times the expected rate [3].
